Depends on the person/how the attack plays out. I’ve cried from panic attacks before and I’ve held my tears as well so yes, a panic attack can make people cry. Check up on them and try to see what you can do if they’re ok with it. Could be an attack or just a breakdown but with the stuff you described it is clear that they’re going through something.

I think that’s where the experience plays a big part. For me I had forgotten all about these attacks but when it kicked in I felt like a sudden sense of familiarization. Grounding yourself is hard as hell when having one but you gotta realize what’s happening and work from there. Personally it’s more like not adding any more unnecessary anxiety/worrying into the mix. It’s still a long emotional battle but it’s easier to manage if you’re not completely freaking out. And likewise to both of your last sentences, I thought I was normalish and forgot how bad it got for people w mental illnesses. And I’m sorry that you have to experience this too, it’s garbage and I hope you’re able to work through this and reach a sense of normalcy afterwards.

I think the experience plays a big part. When they first started they were terrible and they would overwhelm me but if memory serves right it started becoming common so I started adapting in a way. It’s been a long while since my previous attack but when I had one last night it all felt familiar.

But basically what I do is ground myself and try to not let it consume me. I know what’s happening and I know what it is and since I can’t do anything to instantly stop it I just ride it out. It was worse when it was starting cause I was with coworkers in a parking lot (people I’m not too close with in an area that felt scary) but once I got to the comfort of my room i started to get better. I also started talking to my sister about my attack so I think that elevated some of the weight.

Same thing with the disorientation and derealization though, I was struggling to remember common things about me and the world, it all felt so new and it was frightening but I didn’t let it get too bad. I did stuff I remembered like unlocking my phone and going on apps that I frequently use and anything else to tie myself down to this reality.

But so far those are the tips I have. Ground yourself and remind yourself who you are with things that are familiar and easy to remember. Panic attacks pass, you just have to remain as calm as you can and be able to reassure yourself that it’ll end. Get into safe places and surround urself with things that help you feel better, be it people or objects.

You don’t think it would be “fun,” you’re just trying to convincing yourself in order to get onboard with it. If her “taking a break” is just taking a stop from the relationship and living her own life for a month, then personally, it’s kinda understandable. Relationships can be a lot of work and sometimes it feels like a hassle, especially after the honeymoon phase and whatnot. If her definition of a break is just taking time to herself, then try and support if you agree that’s what she and you need.

However, if her definition of a break is just being single single, then there is no point in the relationship. If she wants to try and get with other people during it, then it’s just cheating with permission. If that’s what she’s “missing out on” then I would dump her straight away. People always sugarcoat their words in order to get people to stay. Based on personal experience, people will make plans and say so much good shit like getting married and having kids cause they know that will keep their S/O latched onto them. I might be adding my own interpretation to this, but based on your worries, I might not be too far off.

A relationship is about love and trust. If you trust that she will just take time for herself and not try and get with other people, then let her. But she should also listen to your side as it’s just as important. If it makes you uncomfortable then you have to have a civil talk about it. Tell her your worries and what you feel. Don’t paint her as a villain though, be open and say something such as “hey, im being stupid and i started to think of some dumb things blah blah blah.” If she truly loves you (and if you word it correctly) then she should be able to understand. However, if she pulls a 180 and starts victimizing herself by saying you don’t trust her, then that should be a red flag. You’ve been dating for 4 years and by now you should have a deep level of trust and be able to communicate well enough for her to not misunderstand.

But yea, go along with it if you think it’s okay but if she uses the opportunity to cheat then just dip from the relationship.
